newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: MOTOR RACING-SLOW DINIZ ALLOWED TO RACE.
newsitem.headline: MOTOR RACING-SLOW DINIZ ALLOWED TO RACE.

text.p: Brazilian Pedro Diniz was allowed to race in the season-opening Australian Grand Prix on Sunday even though the Arrows driver failed to clock a time within the minimum qualifying standard.
Diniz, team mate of world champion Damon Hill, had not been fast enough in qualifying on Saturday to record a time within 107 per cent of pole man Jacques Villeneuve's best in his Williams.

But the Arrows team appealed to the race stewards, citing extraordinary difficulties they had experienced during the session and stressing that the Canadian's pole time at Albert Park was also exceptional.
In a statement, the race stewards of the ruling body, the International Motoring Federation (FIA), said they accepted Arrows' argument and allowed Diniz to take part.
Diniz recorded a qualifying time of one minute 35.952 seconds, three-tenths of a secnd outside the cut-off.
Villeneuve set a blistering pace with a lap of one minute 29.369 seconds, almost two seconds quicker than Williams team mate Heinz-Harald Frentzen of Germany.
